newsitem.title: HONG KONG: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - IDBI gives market a try.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - IDBI gives market a try.

text.p: Asian debt markets offered up a few new issues to start the week.
The Industrial Development Bank of India (IDBI) launched its long-anticipated floating rate note (FRN) issue via sole bookrunner Merrill Lynch International.

The US$150 million seven-year FRN pays a coupon of 60 basis points over the six-month London Interbank Offered Rate (LIBOR). The notes were issued and re-offered at 99.460 to give a fixed re-offer yield of LIBOR plus 70 basis points.
The issue will be free to trade from 0900 GMT on Tuesday.

Bankers were more positive on IDBI's seven-year senior straight bond than on Industrial Credit and Investment Corp of India's (ICICI) US$100 million step-up subordinated bond launched last week, saying the pricing for the IDBI issue was more in line with the credit's value.
"We like it. I think we are going to take a piece," said a syndicate manager in Hong Kong, referring to the IDBI deal.

The Philippines' Allied Banking Corp launched a three-year floating rate certificate of deposit (FRCD) that pays an all-in return of 82 basis points, shaving nine basis points off its similar issue launched last November.
ABM Amro Hoare Govett, Fuji International and Standard Chartered Bank are the arrangers.
Schroders Asia launched a HK$500 million FRCD for itself. The paper has final maturity of five years but can be put or called on the third and fourth anniversaries.
With fees, the all-in return is 65 basis points over the Hong Kong Interbank Offered Rate.
Schroders Asia is 75 percent owned by Schroders PLC.
Guangzhou International Trust and Investment Corp was in with a 364-day FRCD that pays an all-in of 115 basis points over LIBOR.
Bankgesellschaft Berlin, Banque Francaise du Commerce Exterieur Singapore, Hana Bank and Kookmin Bank are arrangers.
